schemes.module_code: HUB XC 4xx (e.g. XC421, XC422, XC436, XC438)
schemes.description: BU Hub project-based 4-credit elective, each course co-led by two faculty from different disciplines; interdisciplinary teams of 4-6 undergraduates work with a community partner (faculty, staff, alumni, entrepreneur or nonprofit) on a real-world problem, producing a tangible deliverable (film, podcast, website, work of art etc.) shown at the semi-annual Experiential Learning Expo.
schemes.eligible_faculties_programmes: Open to juniors and seniors from all BU undergraduate schools and colleges
schemes.eligibility_restrictions: Juniors and seniors only; course-specific seat limits; some BU Spark! XC courses require an application
schemes.project_evidence: Teams produce 'a tangible deliverable (film, podcast, website, work of art, etc.)' [2].
schemes.group_evidence: 'interdisciplinary team of undergraduate students'; page lists 'Students per project team' as Four and Six [1][2].
schemes.employer_evidence: A community partner is a standard element of every course and teams present to the partner [2], but partners may be 'faculty, staff, alumni, entrepreneurs, or nonprofits' [2] and listed spring 2026/2027 examples include external organisations (Lawyers for Civil Rights, WalkMassachusetts, Reacting to the Past consortium) alongside internal BU units (Innovate@BU, BU Sustainability TDM) [3][4]. External organisations are therefore not documented as the standard source; per ruling on mixed internal/external clients, C = Unclear.
schemes.partner_role: Community partner defines challenge, collaborates with team, receives final work; share of internal BU partners not quantified
schemes.named_partners: Spring 2026: Lawyers for Civil Rights, WalkMassachusetts, Reacting to the Past consortium (search summary); Spring 2027 listing: WalkMassachusetts, BU Sustainability TDM (internal), Innovate@BU (internal) [3][4]
schemes.deliverable: Tangible deliverable (podcast, film, website, game etc.) plus Expo showcase
schemes.unresolved: Fall 2026 offerings not confirmed; proportion of external vs internal partners unpublished.

profile_md: Boston University has one university-wide employer-linked team route, the Hub Cross-College Challenge (XCC): a 4-credit elective for juniors and seniors from all undergraduate schools in which interdisciplinary teams of four to six work with a community partner and produce a tangible deliverable (podcast, film, website) shown at the Experiential Learning Expo. Partners are a mix of external organisations (Lawyers for Civil Rights, WalkMassachusetts, Reacting to the Past) and internal BU units (Innovate@BU, BU Sustainability), so criterion C is Unclear under the mixed-client ruling. Business provision includes the Questrom Core Innovation Project (live client, teams; deliverable undocumented) and a sponsored MSBA industry capstone (team, industry client, presented to sponsor; meets A, B and C on the page text but undated, so current delivery is unclear). Engineering has a year-long senior design capstone with sponsor-supplied problems (sponsorship reported optional) and the Spark! ML practicum with internal and external partners. MetroBridge links classes to city governments but team/deliverable detail is missing. Provision is distributed across schools rather than institution-wide, and no route is confirmed as meeting all three criteria with current delivery.
gaps: Dated current-year evidence for MSBA capstone, Innovation Project and senior design; external-vs-internal partner share in XCC and DS549; MetroBridge course list; CAS science/humanities departmental projects; PRLab, law clinics and Action Learning Lab not verified; further departmental capstones likely exist (BME, ECE, Hospitality, SPH).
